knowledge_gaps: The diagnostic reliability experiment is a reasonable first step. Originality 4/10 is defensible; potential 8/10 is optimistic without measured incremental fault detection or downstream usefulness. Difficulty 4/10 may underestimate exported-loader integration and exception-safe restoration.

Serving parity can miss defects shared by the model and exported predictor. Specify independent semantic assertions and which implementation each mutation changes; mutating both paths identically could preserve parity.

Mutation detection lacks reproducible criteria: exact fixtures, numerical tolerances, expected detecting probes, proof that each fault was exercised, and treatment of crashes versus semantic detections. Freeze these rules and assess later revisions on unused fixtures.

Outer finally-block restoration is insufficient when exceptions are caught and subsequent probes continue. Restore parameters, buffers, hooks, routing caches and per-module training modes after every probe and mutation. Restoring global RNG state does not restore a consumed loader iterator or its separate generators.

Dependency isolation needs explicit missing-dependency tests that verify completed metrics survive and gate reasons remain accurate. The listed SciPy availability contradicts observed runtime failures; the failing import site and actual execution environment remain unspecified.

No numerical diagnostic budget, fixture count, stopping rule or acceptance criteria are provided. Small synthetic fixtures also cannot establish coverage of realistic histories. Preserve existing behavioral probes and keep qualitative compatibility or present-intent claims separate from measured semantics.
The related-work entries lack verified titles, authors and precise findings. Their applicability and support for the proposed mutation protocol remain uncertain.
